key_insight: Domain-specific biomedical transformer embeddings, especially BioBERT, helped flag clinical trial protocols at higher risk of dosing errors.
clinical_relevance: This approach could support earlier safety screening in trials, helping teams identify problematic dosing descriptions before they affect patients or trial integrity.
method: Encoded clinical trial text with ClinicalBERT, PubMedBERT, BioBERT, and MedCPT.
Combined text embeddings with categorical metadata.
Compared classical ML and neural network classifiers using ROC-AUC.
evidence_signal: BioBERT achieved an ROC-AUC of 0.794 with logistic regression, and the strongest models reached ROC-AUCs of 0.821 to 0.853 for dosing-error prediction.
watch_item: Results come from a model evaluation setting, so real-world performance may differ and needs careful validation before deployment.
paper_title: CaresAI at CT-DEB26: Detecting Dosing Errors In Clinical Trials Using Domain-Specific Transformer Embeddings and Classification Models
